correctness.rationale: The first positive Taylor coefficient of h=(φ−φ(0))^k beyond the offset diameter makes each finite high-cluster compression an invertible lower-triangular Toeplitz block. Lacunary differences have bounded multiplicity, so all off-block interactions have finite squared coefficient sum and their high-column tail is norm small. The resulting coercivity and exponential low-coefficient decay yield HS(β)⊆HS(1). Monotonicity and disjoint lacunary predecessor intervals prove the reverse inclusion when inf nβ_n>0. A fully specified outer function, finite-union Paley inequality, and exact divergent weighted HS series give necessity. Constant symbols are covered by the root condition. The included checker replayed 1518 exact-rational finite assertions; these are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact if-and-only-if Hilbert–Schmidt composition threshold survives finite adjacent/irregular coefficient clusters of size at least two for the entire q>1 Hadamard range, a non-Hadamard sparse geometry that the motivating singleton theorem cannot analyze. It delineates a meaningful boundary for spectral/ideal stability under sparse weighted Hardy perturbations and introduces a reusable block-Toeplitz coercivity principle. Fixed templates, rather than arbitrary chosen slices, arise naturally from bounded-width aggregated frequency exceptions.
